title: Python environment and AWS context / Complete structured CLI inventory
summary: Inspect the supplied evidence and distinguish what each check establishes.

blocks.text: Prepare dependencies and confirm the AWS context before the supplied automation script runs.
An application’s virtual environment isolates its interpreter context and installed Python packages.
Create the environment with python -m venv ENV_DIR. Activate it with your platform’s command; on Unix, for example, use source ENV_DIR/bin/activate.
Inside the environment, install supplied requirements with python -m pip install -r requirements.txt. Inspect packages with python -m pip list, then use that interpreter for the supplied script.
Before AWS automation runs, confirm the approved AWS profile and Region through the supplied credential configuration.

items.text:
Unix record:
python -m venv ENV_DIR
source ENV_DIR/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip list
Context check: supplied approved AWS profile and Region match.
python <supplied_script_filename>
Record: supplied outcome successful; ENV_DIR interpreter used throughout; global packages unchanged.

Unix record: ENV_DIR created but inactive. requirements.txt installed with the host interpreter; packages listed globally. Approved AWS context confirmed. Script then runs with the host interpreter.
Conclusion: isolated execution verified.

Record: ENV_DIR active; dependencies installed and listed there; script runs successfully using ENV_DIR. Only afterward does the operator compare profile and Region with the approved credential configuration.
Conclusion: ready-before-run checks met.

i1.message: The record shows activation, environment-scoped installation and inspection, separate AWS context confirmation and execution with that interpreter.

i2.message: AWS context confirmation does not correct global installation and execution outside the isolated environment.

i3.message: The approved profile and Region must be confirmed before AWS automation executes.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

blocks.text: An inventory needs complete results from the approved account and Region.
For supported commands, AWS CLI follows service-side pagination automatically unless automatic pagination is disabled.
For structured inventory, specify --profile, --region and --output json. Leave out --no-paginate when you need the full listing.
--page-size adjusts service-call page size, not total output count. --max-items bounds output; retain a returned NextToken and use --starting-token to collect the remainder manually.

Keep explicit profile, Region and JSON output on the supplied supported inventory command. A full listing keeps automatic pagination enabled. A deliberately bounded --max-items listing retains NextToken for --starting-token continuation. Preserve continuation evidence with the inventory.
Smaller service pages do not imply fewer total results. --page-size and --max-items control different limits; manual continuation must not discard NextToken.

blocks.title: Complete structured CLI inventory
blocks.alt_text: Automatic collection follows requests and responses until no results remain. Bounded --max-items collection resumes NextToken with --starting-token, keeping the same explicit profile and Region. --page-size changes service-call size, not total output.

steps.title: A closer look: Complete structured CLI inventory

segments.label: How the AWS CLI collects a full listing across service pages
segments.summary: A supported listing operation can require several service requests rather than one. Using an EC2 snapshot listing as the example, the speaker explains that each response indicates whether more results remain. The AWS CLI automatically requests subsequent pages until the service reports no more results, then assembles the complete list in memory and returns it as command output.

blocks.group_title: How automatic pagination builds a complete inventory

bridge.before: Watch how service responses tell the AWS CLI whether another page is needed, and how automatic pagination assembles those pages into one listing.
bridge.after: The clip explains automatic collection, but not disabling it, explicit profile/Region/JSON settings, or page-size, output-limit, and token-resumption controls. The text covers those requirements for a complete, consistently scoped inventory.

public.prompt: A bounded inventory call returns NextToken. Which interpretation and next step are correct?

options.text: --page-size controls service-call page size; retain NextToken and resume with --starting-token in the same explicit profile and Region to collect the remainder.
--page-size fixes the total output count, so the token can be discarded.
--max-items changes only the service-call page size; start again without the token.

o1.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o2.message: --page-size does not bound the total count, and a returned continuation must be retained.

o3.message: --max-items bounds output; restarting without the continuation does not resume the remainder.

correct.message: Your choice follows the stated evidence and verification rule.

items.text:
Supported inventory command: explicit approved --profile and --region, --output json; neither --no-paginate nor --max-items on full export. Automatic collection completes.
Bounded exercise: --page-size controls service calls; --max-items bounds output. Each returned NextToken retained and passed as --starting-token on the next call with the same profile, Region and JSON format, until no continuation remains.

Full export: explicit approved profile, Region, JSON, plus --no-paginate.
Bounded exercise: every NextToken retained and resumed in the same context.
Conclusion: full-listing and continuation requirements both met.

Full export: automatic pagination, explicit approved profile and Region, JSON, no output limit.
Bounded exercise: --max-items returns NextToken; operator discards it, claiming --page-size already fixed the total output count.

i1.message: Both full automatic collection and same-context manual continuation are present, with the two limits distinguished.

i2.message: Correct manual continuation does not fix disabling automatic pagination on the full-listing export.

i3.message: The token is needed for resumption, and --page-size controls service-call size rather than total output.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Separate service-call sizing from total-output limits and follow every continuation.
